posts.title: Ask questions about a Google Sheet
posts.promise: Build a small workflow that answers questions from one prepared spreadsheet.
posts.whatItIs: This n8n template connects a chat interface to Google Sheets and an AI model so someone can ask questions about spreadsheet data. It describes detecting column meanings and keeping conversation context for follow-up questions. A small version could support one sheet with a few clearly defined questions instead of trying to analyze any spreadsheet.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: a small team that repeatedly checks the same spreadsheet may pay for a focused question-answer workflow. The template does not establish customers or demand.
loop: A person prepares a Google Sheet with clear column names.
A question arrives through the chat interface.
The workflow reads the relevant sheet data and column descriptions.
The model drafts an answer using that data and prior conversation context.
A person checks the answer against the sheet before relying on it.
The workflow keeps context for a follow-up question.
posts.evidence: The n8n template page describes a Google Sheets chatbot using an OpenAI model, natural-language questions, column detection, and conversation memory. It gives setup directions and says its sample data uses a header row and rows 2–100. This documents a workflow template, not customer use or business results.
posts.uncertainty: A student version could use one test sheet and a narrow set of questions. The source does not establish answer accuracy or customer demand. Spreadsheet permissions, API credentials, changing columns, and incorrect answers require human oversight; verify every answer before acting on it.
first24Hours: Create a test sheet with a header row and a few sample records.
Import the template into an n8n account and connect the required services.
Try five known questions and compare every answer with the sheet.

ease.reason: The template provides a concrete starting workflow and sheet format; service credentials still require setup.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams repeating spreadsheet lookups may pay; this template supplies no demand evidence.

feasibility.reason: A one-sheet, narrow-question prototype is plausible in two weeks; accuracy and changing data need testing.

autonomy.reason: The workflow answers repeat queries, while a person must validate outputs before using them.

evidence.reason: The first-party page documents workflow steps and setup, but does not establish customer outcomes.

steps.message: Assessed eight enriched selected leads using attached evidence and recent-post comparisons. Picked the distinct n8n spreadsheet question-answer workflow at the five-point mean of 6.2; other candidates were excluded for limited evidence, scope, duplication, or weaker buyer support.
